title: LED Bar Graph
description: Turn a knob and watch a 10-segment bar graph fill up like a level meter.

steps.clip: You need: an Arduino Uno and its USB cable, a breadboard, 1 × 10-segment LED bar graph, 10 × 220 Ω resistor, 1 × knob (10 kΩ potentiometer), and some jumper wires.
Push the bar graph in across the middle gap: ten legs above the gap, ten below. The printed side (the + legs) goes on top.
hints: Each of the ten bars is its own little LED: + leg on top, − leg below the gap.
steps.goal: Put the bar graph across the middle gap.

steps.clip: Run a wire from bar 1's + leg (top half) to pin 2 on the Arduino.
hints: Any hole in that column works.
steps.goal: Connect bar 1's + leg to pin 2.

steps.clip:
Two things:
1. A wire from the Arduino's GND pin to the blue − row at the bottom.
2. Stand a 220 Ω resistor upright: one leg in bar 1's − column (row h), the other leg in the blue − row just below it.
hints: Each bar needs its own resistor, like any LED.
steps.goal: Connect bar 1's − leg to GND through a 220 Ω resistor.

steps.goal: Connect bar 2's + leg to pin 3.

hints: The − row has a small gap under bar 6, so its resistor stands in column 11 instead.
steps.goal: Connect bar 6's − leg to GND through a 220 Ω resistor.

steps.clip: Push the knob into the breadboard, each of its three legs in its own column.
hints: The two outer legs are for power; the middle leg gives the reading.
steps.goal: Put the knob on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from one outer leg of the knob to the blue − row.
hints: Either outer leg works.
steps.goal: Connect one outer leg of the knob to GND.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's 5V pin → the red + row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. The knob's other outer leg → that same row.
hints: Now the knob has 0 V at one end and 5 V at the other.
steps.goal: Connect the knob's other outer leg to 5V.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the knob's middle leg to pin A0 on the Arduino.
hints: Pin A0 is on the ANALOG IN side of the Arduino.
The middle leg's voltage follows the knob: 0 V to 5 V.
steps.goal: Connect the knob's middle leg to pin A0.

steps.clip: Copy the code into the Arduino IDE and click Upload. Turn the knob: the bar fills up from one end to the other.
